records.d: YouTube, founded in 2005, let anyone broadcast to the world: the creator era began. Audience became something you could earn from a bedroom. The influencer's stage was built.
records.h: User-uploaded video with revenue sharing turned viewers into broadcasters. The gatekeepers lost the gate. The platform was the studio.
records.mj: Established - documented 2005 founding; user-broadcast video platform.

records.d: Twitter, launched in 2006, gave everyone a real-time audience: thoughts broadcast to followers instantly. Personality became a feed. The influencer gained a direct line.
records.h: Short public posts with follow mechanics built audiences around voice rather than production. The feed was the medium. Influence became measurable in followers.
records.mj: Established - documented 2006 launch; real-time social broadcasting.

records.d: Instagram, launched in October 2010, made the curated visual life the influencer medium: photos as personal brand. The feed became a portfolio. Influence went visual.
records.h: Mobile photo sharing with filters turned daily life into styled content. Brands saw the billboard. The square photo became the ad unit.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2010 launch; visual influencer platform.

records.d: By 2012, influencer agencies and networks were forming: talent management for social creators. The influencer became a profession with representation. The bedroom broadcaster got an agent.
records.h: Agencies packaged creators for brand deals, handling contracts and pricing. The business professionalized. Influence became inventory.
records.mj: Established - documented agency formation era; influencer marketing professionalizes.

records.d: Vine's stars in 2013 proved six seconds could build a career: short video as influence. Brands paid for loops. Brevity became bankable.
records.h: Six-second looping videos with massive teen audiences attracted brand integrations. The format was the constraint. Short attention became the product.
records.mj: Established - documented 2013 Vine star economy; short-video influence.

records.d: Multi-channel networks peaked around 2014, rolling up YouTube creators into managed portfolios: the influencer as portfolio asset. Scale met the creator. The network owned the audience relationship.
records.h: MCNs offered production, sales, and advances in exchange for revenue shares across creator portfolios. Consolidation followed. The creator became an asset class.
records.mj: Established - documented MCN era; creator portfolios consolidated.

records.d: By 2015, sponsored posts had standardized: rate cards, media kits, engagement metrics. The influencer post became a media buy. Authenticity got a price list.
records.h: Standard metrics, reach, engagement rate, CPM, let brands buy influence like ad inventory. The post was the unit. The market matured.
records.mj: Established - documented standardization; sponsored posts as media buys.

records.d: In 2016, the short-video era consolidated around TikTok: algorithmic feeds making anyone viral overnight. The algorithm became the kingmaker. Followers mattered less than the For You page.
records.h: Recommendation algorithms served content to non-followers, decoupling reach from audience size. Virality democratized. The feed was the star-maker.
records.mj: Established - documented 2016 era; algorithmic short-video feeds.

records.d: In 2016, the first CGI influencers began posting like human creators: outfit photos, brand tags, fan replies. The influencer went synthetic. The feed accepted a fictional person.
records.h: Rendered personas maintained posting schedules and storylines, engaging followers who debated their reality. The content was the same; the creator was software. The industry noted the engagement.
records.mj: Established - documented 2016 virtual influencer debuts; synthetic creators posting.
records.z: timeline|year=2016|span=1|events=first CGI influencers post~the feed accepts fiction

records.d: By 2017, disclosure enforcement was reshaping influencer marketing: #ad tags, clear labeling, platform tools. Transparency became law. The industry learned that trust needs labels.
records.h: Regulators required clear disclosure of paid relationships, with platforms adding branded-content tools. Compliance became workflow. The label protected the market.
records.mj: Established - documented disclosure enforcement era; influencer transparency rules.

records.d: In 2018, the follower-fraud reckoning hit: brands discovered bought followers and fake engagement, demanding verification. The audience had to be real. Authenticity became auditable.
records.h: Audit tools exposed bot followers and engagement pods, shifting budgets to vetted creators. Measurement matured. The industry priced honesty.
records.mj: Established - documented 2018 fraud reckoning; influencer verification.

records.d: By 2019, virtual influencers were fronting fashion campaigns: magazine covers, runway appearances, brand ambassadorships. Fiction wore couture. The industry embraced the synthetic muse.
records.h: Luxury and streetwear brands cast CGI personas for campaigns, valuing control and novelty. The muse was software. Fashion's future face was rendered.
records.mj: Established - documented campaigns; virtual influencers in fashion.
records.z: timeline|year=2019|span=1|events=virtual influencers front fashion campaigns~fiction wears couture

records.d: In 2020, platforms launched creator funds paying for views: TikTok, Snapchat, and others funded the feed directly. The platform became the patron. Creation got a salary.
records.h: Funds distributed payments based on view performance, professionalizing full-time creation. The algorithm paid. The creator economy gained payroll.
records.mj: Established - documented 2020 creator funds; platform-paid creation.

records.d: In 2021, analysts sized the creator economy above $100 billion: 50 million creators as a labor force. Influence became macroeconomics. The bedroom broadcaster was an industry.
records.h: Market sizing counted creators, platforms, and services as an economy larger than many nations' media sectors. Investment followed. The economy was real.
records.mj: Established - documented 2021 analyses; creator economy above $100 billion.

records.d: By 2021, AI writing assistants were drafting creators' captions, scripts, and posts: the influencer's first AI staff. The caption got a co-writer. Creation's busywork automated.
records.h: Language models generated post copy from briefs, with creators editing and publishing. The workflow was human-led, AI-assisted. The assistant joined the team.
records.mj: Emerging - real products; AI writing assistants for creators.

records.d: By 2022, agencies were managing rosters of virtual influencers like talent stables: casting synthetic faces for campaigns. The model agency went digital. The roster was rendered.
records.h: Agencies built and managed CGI personas, selling their endorsements to brands. The business mirrored modeling agencies. Talent became intellectual property.
records.mj: Emerging - real agencies; managed virtual influencer rosters.

records.d: By 2022, AI was producing creator content at scale: generated videos, voices, and posts flooding feeds. Volume became cheap. The feed's supply curve broke.
records.h: Generative pipelines produced endless variations of content for testing and posting. Creators became directors of output. The bottleneck moved from production to taste.
records.mj: Emerging - real practice; AI content pipelines for creators.

records.d: By 2023, AI influencers were operating as real businesses: subscription revenue, brand deals, and fan payments flowing to synthetic persons. The P&L was real. Fiction had cash flow.
records.h: AI personas monetized through fan platforms and sponsorships, with small teams operating them profitably. The economics worked. The business model was proven.
records.mj: Emerging - real reported revenues; AI influencer businesses.
records.z: formula|label=AI influencer monthly revenue (EUR, reported cases)|a=10000|b=1|op=mul|unit=euros

records.d: By 2023, AI-generated UGC creators were filming 'authentic' product reviews without existing: synthetic customers recommending products. The testimonial went synthetic. Trust's raw material was manufactured.
records.h: AI avatars delivered scripted reviews styled as user content for brands. Disclosure varied. The format borrowed UGC's trust. Authenticity became a production choice.
records.mj: Emerging - real practice; AI-generated UGC-style creators.

records.d: In September 2023, TikTok began labeling AI-generated content: the platform marked synthetic media. The feed learned to tag fiction. Disclosure became interface.
records.h: Detection and self-labeling tools marked AI-made videos for viewers. The label was the compromise between ban and chaos. Transparency became a UI element.
records.mj: Established - documented September 2023 TikTok policy; AI content labels.
records.z: timeline|year=2023|span=1|events=TikTok labels AI content~disclosure becomes interface

records.d: By 2024, AI livestream sellers were hosting shopping broadcasts: synthetic hosts pitching products for hours without tiring. The infomercial host became software. Commerce's hardest shift automated.
records.h: AI avatars with product knowledge ran live shopping shows, answering questions and demonstrating goods. The shift never ended. The host was tireless.
records.mj: Emerging - real deployments; AI livestream shopping hosts.

records.d: By 2024, fully AI-run influencer accounts were operating: content planned, produced, and posted by pipelines with minimal human touch. The creator was the software. The account ran itself.
records.h: Agentic pipelines handled ideation, production, posting, and community management, with humans in oversight. The workflow was end-to-end. The influencer became an operation.
records.mj: Emerging - real operations; AI-run influencer accounts.

records.d: By 2025, platforms were letting brands cast AI influencers like stock photos: searchable synthetic talent for campaigns. The influencer became inventory. Casting went to a search bar.
records.h: Marketplaces listed AI personas with audience stats and rates, bookable for campaigns. The transaction was instant. Talent became searchable.
records.mj: Emerging - real platforms; AI influencer casting marketplaces.

records.d: By 2025, brands were deploying synthetic spokespeople as permanent faces: always-on, scandal-proof ambassadors. The mascot became a person. The brand face never aged.
records.h: Persistent AI personas represented brands across channels, with consistent voice and memory of customer interactions. The ambassador was forever. The face was forever.
records.mj: Emerging - real deployments; synthetic brand spokespeople.

records.d: By 2025, experiments were letting audiences co-own AI creators: fans voting on persona decisions and sharing revenue. The influencer became a cooperative. Fandom gained equity.
records.h: Tokenized or contractual models gave fans governance over AI persona direction and a share of earnings. The audience was the board. The creator was collective.
records.mj: Emerging - real experiments; audience-owned AI creators.
